benchmark: C4 (en) validation perplexity -- the NON-WIKITEXT-OVERLAPPING evaluation
purpose: QAT trains on a WikiText-2 train blend and is scored on WikiText-2 test. There is no split leakage, but the training domain matches the eval domain, so a WikiText-2 result partly measures domain alignment rather than quantization quality. C4 is web text from a different distribution and contributes nothing to the training mix, so it tests whether a WikiText-2 gain generalizes. Companion to results/wikitext2_perplexity.json; the two tables are kept separate by design.

harness.corpus_source: allenai/c4, en/c4-validation.00000-of-00008.json.gz, documents taken in file order until ~1.29 M chars (deterministic). Rebuild with: scripts/prepare_eval_data.py --datasets c4
harness.note: Corpus sized to match wikitext2_test.txt (1,290,546 chars / 583 chunks) so the two evaluations have comparable chunk counts and error-bar widths. All four rows below used this identical harness.

results.label: QAT Q2_K, CAKLD + ptq_q2k init + WikiText/Alpaca blend (the 26.95 best)
QAT Q2_K, same but Alpaca-only (--wikitext-frac 0), the 70.88 result
PTQ Q2_K (llama-quantize on the unmodified base model)

superseded_value.reason: untied build: Q2_K token_embd with a separate Q6_K output.weight

results.why_changed: PTQ involves no training; this reflects a quantization-recipe change. scripts/quantize_ptq.sh now passes --token-embedding-type f16 --output-tensor-type f16 and drops the duplicate output.weight, so the PTQ baseline carries the same F16 tied embedding as the QAT export in place of a Q2_K embedding with a separate Q6_K output head. Both 2-bit variants are now 310 tensors / 0.5960 B elements with identical tensor names, leaving quality as the variable under test. Measured 2026-08-04; the prior value describes the superseded build recorded under superseded_value.

results.label: QAT Q2_K, batch 24, wikitext-frac 0.05 + FineWeb 0.5 blend, final checkpoint (step 48828)
results.role: Current best on C4 (and on WikiText2, see results/wikitext2_perplexity.json), replacing qat_q2k_blend (55.9509 on C4, 1.90x fp16). The ratio_to_fp16_* fields above are measured against the never-fine-tuned fp16 base model, which is not a fair ceiling since that baseline never saw this run's training data. Treat them as raw data rather than as support for a 'beats fp16' or 'closes the fp16 gap' claim; see analysis.batch24_fineweb_scaleup.fp16_ceiling_status. The validated comparisons are against the prior QAT recipe (qat_q2k_blend) and against PTQ, both like-for-like.

results.label: QAT Q2_K, batch 24, wikitext-frac 0.05 + FineWeb 0.5 blend, safety-net checkpoint (step 47500)
results.role: Statistically indistinguishable from qat_q2k_fineweb_final (overlapping stderr). Retained for the record; see results/wikitext2_perplexity.json's analysis.batch24_fineweb_scaleup for why this checkpoint was measured (the step-20000 trough checkpoint was not available) and why the final checkpoint is the one to promote.

analysis.headline: About half the WikiText blend's apparent advantage is domain alignment, not quantization quality. The blend-vs-Alpaca-only spread is 2.63x on WikiText-2 (26.95 vs 70.88) but only 1.31x on C4 (55.95 vs 73.03).

off_domain_degradation.note: Measured against fp16 on the same corpus, the best QAT model loses substantially more ground on C4 than on WikiText-2.
off_domain_degradation.implication: The WikiText-2 headline number overstates this checkpoint's general quality. Quote the C4 ratio alongside it, or the 2-bit cost reads as roughly half its off-domain value.

ptq_control.note: PTQ is never trained, so it has no domain adaptation to inflate its WikiText-2 score. Its degradation ratio is essentially unchanged across the two corpora: 10.34x on WikiText-2 against 9.48x on C4. Updated 2026-08-04 for the embedding-tying change, from 12.91x / 12.28x; the qualitative point, near-equal ratios across corpora, is unaffected.
ptq_control.why_it_matters: This rules out the alternative explanation that C4 is simply harder in a way that penalizes low-bit models generally. C4 is harder in absolute terms (fp16 moves 21.37 -> 29.46), but that difficulty affects the fp16 denominator too. Only the trained models' ratios move, which localizes the effect to their training data rather than to the corpus.
ptq_control._note_before_2026_08_04: PTQ is never trained, so it has no domain adaptation to inflate its WikiText-2 score. Its degradation ratio is essentially unchanged across the two corpora -- 12.91x on WikiText-2 vs 12.28x on C4.

qat_vs_ptq_off_domain.note: QAT outperforms PTQ substantially off-domain. Against the current best QAT (qat_q2k_fineweb_final): 32.19 vs 279.30 on C4, an 8.68x gap, and 18.46 vs 220.93 on WikiText-2, an 11.97x gap. Updated 2026-08-04, when PTQ was re-measured following the embedding-tying change; the prior note compared the then-current best QAT of 55.95 against PTQ 361.61 for a 6.46x C4 gap.
qat_vs_ptq_off_domain.verdict: The central claim -- 2-bit QAT preserves substantially more quality than 2-bit PTQ at the same bit-width -- holds on a corpus neither model was trained toward. The margin is smaller than WikiText-2 suggests and remains substantial.
qat_vs_ptq_off_domain._note_before_2026_08_04: QAT still beats PTQ decisively off-domain: 55.95 vs 361.61, a 6.46x gap on C4 (vs 10.24x on WikiText-2).

alpaca_only_domain_neutrality.note: The Alpaca-only model moves little in absolute terms (70.88 WikiText-2 -> 73.03 C4) and improves relative to fp16 (3.32x -> 2.48x).
alpaca_only_domain_neutrality.why: It never saw WikiText-2 train text, so it had no domain advantage to lose. Its WikiText-2 score was, in effect, already an out-of-domain measurement.

analysis.caveat_c4_and_pretraining: C4 is a common LLM pretraining corpus, so Qwen3-0.6B's base weights may well have seen C4-derived text. That affects all four rows equally (they share the same base model) and so does not bias the comparison between them, but it means C4 is 'not in the QAT fine-tuning mix', not 'never seen by the model'.

batch24_fineweb_scaleup.note: Cross-reference: full writeup and training-time-proxy-trough caveat is in results/wikitext2_perplexity.json's analysis.batch24_fineweb_scaleup. This is the C4 (held-out generalization) half of that result.
batch24_fineweb_scaleup.headline: C4 improved more in relative terms than WikiText2: C4 -42.4% (55.95 -> 32.25) against WikiText2 -31.4% (26.95 -> 18.49). This run traded WikiText-2-specific training data (frac 0.5 -> 0.05) for general FineWeb data (frac 0 -> 0.5), so a larger C4 gain than WikiText2 gain is the signal it was designed to test: the improvement reflects generalization from more diverse training data rather than domain-alignment inflation, which would instead appear as a WikiText2-skewed gain.
batch24_fineweb_scaleup.fp16_ceiling_status: The ratio_to_fp16_c4 / ratio_to_fp16_wikitext2 fields on the two new rows are computed against fp16_raw, the base model, never fine-tuned on this run's Alpaca+WikiText2+FineWeb blend. That is not a fair ceiling for a 'does QAT beat or approach fp16' claim: fp16_raw had no opportunity to adapt to this data while the QAT model trained on it for 48828 steps, so some or all of the apparent narrowing (to 1.09x on C4, and 0.87x on WikiText2) may be a domain-adaptation effect rather than evidence about the cost of 2-bit quantization. A fair ceiling -- fp16 fine-tuned on the identical blend for the same step count -- has not been run, and further GPU budget was not allocated to it. Until that ceiling exists, treat the ratio_to_fp16_* fields as raw data rather than as support for an fp16 comparison in either direction.
batch24_fineweb_scaleup.fineweb_c4_overlap: FineWeb (a Common Crawl derivative) and C4 (also Common Crawl derived, built entirely from the CC-MAIN-2019-18 snapshot per the FineWeb paper, arXiv:2406.17557) could in principle share content, which would make part of the C4 generalization gain the same domain-leakage effect the WikiText2/C4 split was designed to catch, routed through FineWeb. Checked directly: re-streamed the exact FineWeb slice consumed in training (32,236 docs, deterministic, reproduced identically on a second re-stream) and the exact 613 C4 eval docs. Result: 0 of the 32,236 FineWeb docs came from CC-MAIN-2019-18 (this sample-10BT pull spans 8 other dumps, 2013-2022); 0 exact URL matches; 0 documents met FineWeb's own near-duplicate bar (word 5-gram shingle overlap >=75%). The highest containment was 53.5%, and inspection of every match above 10% showed template and boilerplate overlap -- alumni-directory software templates, generic terms-of-service language -- rather than shared substantive content. This covers the specific slices used rather than the full corpora: full FineWeb does structurally contain C4's source snapshot, so a run streaming a different portion of FineWeb should repeat this check.
